title: Structured patient-centered decision support for resource planning of interventional endoscopic procedures in the border area of ​​outpatient or inpatient intervention - a data-based approach from the AHEAD project (Application-oriented Healthcare Development Environment)
summary:
The study is planned and carried out by the II. Medical Clinic of the University Medical Center Mannheim. A total of 270 patients are expected to take part in the study.

Background:
For gastroscopies and colonoscopies with surgery, a decision must be made as to whether the patient has to stay in the clinic for observation or whether they can go home the same day. This decision depends on many individual factors (e.g. previous illnesses, blood-thinning medications, the course of the procedure, the symptoms after the procedure and the patient's situation at home). So far, this decision has been made primarily based on experience. This can lead to patients being hospitalized unnecessarily or, conversely, inpatient monitoring being overlooked. We would like to find out whether a new, structured computer system (AHEAD system) can help to bring together the necessary information completely, clearly and reliably.
Question and objective:
This study is just a feasibility study (pilot study). In this study, we do not yet want to examine whether the system provides better medical care to patients. First of all, we just want to check whether the data collection works well in the clinic's everyday life, how doctors and nursing staff cope with it and how reliable the data collected is. Only if the AHEAD system proves to be suitable in this pilot study will a larger study on its medical effectiveness be planned.
A second important goal of the study is to compile an anonymized data set. This is used to further improve a learning computer program (a so-called classifier). This program will later – in a future, separate study – support doctors in deciding whether to provide outpatient or inpatient follow-up care. In the current pilot study, this program is expressly not being used for your treatment.
Methodology:
The study is expected to last 30 days for each participant.
The study will run for a total of 17 to 18 weeks and is divided into three consecutive phases. Each patient never takes part in exactly one phase.
In phase 1, patients are treated as before. The AHEAD system is not yet used at this stage. The study only evaluates the information that is already documented in the medical file as part of your normal treatment.
In phase 2 the AHEAD system is used. The treating doctor enters information about the procedure into the system in a structured manner. There is no summary display for the treatment team at this stage.
In Phase 3, the AHEAD system is now fully active. In addition, the treatment team sees a simple, colored overview (red, yellow, green) with the most important information. This overview is based on fixed, comprehensible rules (e.g. previous illnesses, blood-thinning medication, duration of the procedure, symptoms afterwards). This is not a recommendation from a learning program. The decision about outpatient or inpatient follow-up care is still made exclusively by the treating doctor.
conditions: Colorectal and esophageal adenomas and early carcinomas; esophageal strictures; choledocholithiasis; and benign and malignant biliary strictures.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned interventional endoscopic procedure: ERCP (Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography), EUS-FNB (Endosonographic Fine Needle Biopsy), Polypectomy (≥1 cm), EMR (Endoscopic Mucosal Resection), ESD (Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection), Esophageal Dilatation/Bouging, other interventional procedures at the discretion of the PI

Procedure in the outpatient/inpatient border area (i.e. the decision to hospitalize is clinically relevant)

Capacity to consent: Patient is capable of consent and can give informed consent

Language skills: sufficient knowledge of the german language for use of the patient portal (or availability of a translator)
Exclusion criteria:
Emergency procedures: Acute emergencies in which hospitalization is already certain before the procedure

Planned hospitalization: Patients for whom hospitalization has already been determined for other reasons (e.g. other illness, planned further procedure)

Lack of ability to consent: Patients who are unable to give consent (e.g. dementia, acute confusion)

Refusal to participate in the study: Patient refuses to participate

Technical impossibility: Patient cannot use patient portal (e.g. no smartphone/computer, no internet connection) and no support available

Withdrawal of consent: Patient withdraws consent

Protocol Violation: Major protocol violation

Security Concerns: Unexpected security issues
